tagline: We facilitate self-paced learning for knowledge seekers.
description: Knowledge InSight publishes self-paced programs for curious minds. You bring the curiosity; we provide the structure, sequence, and guiding questions.
splashLede: Knowledge InSight publishes free, self-paced programs for curious minds. Every program is designed end to end: sequenced readings, guided conversation with an AI assistant, reflective writing, and self-scored checks you can take as often as you like.
about: Knowledge InSight makes self-paced learning experiences for curious people who want to go deeper into a subject for their own sake. There is no enrolment, no cohort, and no deadline. You bring the curiosity; we provide the structure, sequence, and guiding questions.

Our programs are open access and self-paced. Nothing is graded. Quizzes score themselves and can be retaken without limit. Written work stays with you, in your own notebook or document; we never collect it.

Each program is organized as a small number of courses, each course as modules, and each module as lessons. A lesson is one sitting. The structure repeats so you can settle into it and spend your attention on the material instead of the interface.
aboutAside: When it comes to AI in education, I view myself as a critical optimist — someone who remains enthusiastic about the potential of AI, yet alert to the many difficult questions it raises. This project explores AI's positive potential with a focus on quality, starting with topics I'm currently interested in myself.
progressHeading: How to progress through a program
progressLede: Every lesson has the same shape, so you can settle into it and spend your attention on the material.

principles.title: Read first
principles.body: Ideas arrive as prose you can engage with. References name the sources, note free-to-access versions when available, and link to the text or publisher so you can explore further.

principles.title: Think out loud
principles.body: AI-driven Guided Conversations run in your own AI account. Prompts are written to ask, not to tell, and to correct misreadings while guiding your understanding.

principles.title: Check yourself
principles.body: Knowledge checks are ungraded and unlimited. Every option carries its own feedback, so a wrong answer teaches you something specific as you progress in your understanding.

principles.title: Keep your work
principles.body: Journals, activities, and course projects are yours. There is no upload, no submission, and no account. Your progress is remembered by your browser alone.

ai.heading: AI in education
intro: Our programs are developed with the help of generative AI, and we would rather tell you exactly how than leave you guessing.

A learning designer works iteratively with an AI assistant to design the program structure, the course outlines, and the learning objectives. Once that scaffolding is settled, the designer uses AI to draft the learning content against those outlines. Every reading names its sources and links to them wherever they are freely available, so you can go to the original instead of taking a summary on trust. That is the point of the links: not decoration, but a standing invitation to check the work.
vetting: A fully vetted program has completed human-in-the-loop review: a subject-matter expert has validated every learning item and every source in it.

An in-progress program is published while that review is still underway. We release early because the material is useful early, and because readers catch things that reviewers miss. Every page of an in-progress program says so, and tells you how to report what you find.
conversations: We also leverage AI to help facilitate your learning journey. Each Guided Conversation is a prompt written and reviewed by the learning designer. It tells the assistant to ask rather than lecture, to keep its turns short, to treat your observations as evidence, and to correct a specific list of misreadings that the material tends to invite.
You run it in your own account, so the conversation belongs to you. We never see it. You can open the same prompt in Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM of your choice.

Nothing in a Guided Conversation is graded or recorded. If the assistant says something that contradicts the readings, trust the readings and tell us. Remember that the LLM model you use will impact the quality of the conversation.

bio.name: Adam Hodges, Ph.D.
bio.text: Knowledge InSight is an experimental project developed by Adam Hodges, a scholar, professor and learning design consultant with over two decades of experience in higher education — including several years working internationally to develop and deliver American university curriculum to a global audience.

vetted.label: Fully vetted
vetted.blurb: A subject-matter expert has reviewed and validated every learning item and source in this program.

in-progress.label: Vetting in progress
in-progress.blurb: This program is published while expert review is still underway. The content is complete and the sources are linked, but it has not yet been validated end to end.
in-progress.helpLede: You are reading it closely anyway. If something looks wrong, please tell us to help improve the program.
helpPoints: Check claims against the linked sources. Every reading names where its ideas come from. If a passage misstates a source, or attributes something to the wrong thinker, say so and point to the item.
Report broken or wrong links. Free editions move and paywalls change. A dead link is worth reporting even when the text around it is fine.
Flag quiz questions that do not hold up. An answer you can defend that is marked wrong, an option with no good answer, or feedback that misses the point.
Suggest improvements. A passage that reads as muddled, an example that would land better, a primary text we should have pointed you to.

programs.title: AI Literacy
programs.subtitle: Understand how AI models work, use them well in your own work, and judge the arguments about them.
programs.summary: An open-access, self-paced program on how large language models work, how to use them ethically and productively, and the controversies around them.
programs.description:
AI assistants now draft, summarize, and advise for millions of people, and most of us use them without knowing what is happening behind the answers. This program starts there. It explains, in words and with no math or code, how a language model learns from text, how a trained model becomes an assistant, and why fluent answers can still be wrong.

From there it turns to your own use: testing a model on the tasks you care about, checking what it tells you, and setting rules for disclosure, privacy, and dependence. It closes with the arguments that fill the news, from alignment and safety to jobs, copyright, and regulation, each put in the form its strongest advocates would accept. Each course ends with a project of your own: explaining one model answer, writing and testing an AI-use protocol, and mapping a live controversy.
programs.audience: Anyone who can hold a conversation with an AI chatbot and wants to understand, use, and judge these tools. No technical or policy background is assumed.
outcomes: Explain how a language model learns from text, becomes an assistant, and produces fluent errors
Test a model on your own tasks and verify the claims, sources, and citations in what it gives you
Use AI for writing, analysis, and delegated work with rules for disclosure, privacy, and dependence that keep your judgment in charge
Weigh the competing claims about AI safety, work, information, creative rights, and governance, and state the strongest case on each side

programs.title: Phenomenology for Consciousness Studies
programs.subtitle: Trace phenomenology from Husserl to Merleau-Ponty and apply it to today's consciousness debates.
programs.summary: An open-access, self-paced program running from Husserl through Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty to current consciousness studies.
programs.description:
Phenomenology began as a demand: go back to the things themselves, and describe experience as it is actually given rather than as our theories say it must be. This program follows that demand from Husserl's founding method through Heidegger's and Merleau-Ponty's existential and embodied revisions, and into the consciousness research that now draws on all three.

You will work through intentionality, the epoche and reduction, time-consciousness, being-in-the-world, the body-subject, and the hard problem, and you will finish each course by writing something of your own: a phenomenological description, an analysis of a skilled activity, an essay on the body-subject, and a position paper on consciousness.
programs.audience: Curious readers at advanced undergraduate level and beyond, comfortable following an argument across a long text. No prior study of phenomenology or Kant is assumed.
outcomes: Describe an experience phenomenologically, using the epoche, eidetic variation, and the noesis-noema structure
Trace how Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty reworked Husserl's project and what each change cost and gained
Analyze skilled, embodied activity in the vocabulary of being-in-the-world and the body-subject
Position yourself in current debates on consciousness, from the hard problem to enactive and predictive accounts
